title: Ancient Acoustics Laboratory
description: Students explore how sound energy propagates through an ancient Celtic temple by placing and configuring BoomBox speakers at strategic positions around the Nemetona shrine. They must balance total acoustic energy across five sacred zones while respecting a conservation law that caps the system's total wattage, using undo/redo to refine placements and coupled frequency-volume sliders to achieve resonance targets.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load nemetona.glb as a central ancient shrine on a ground plane and load BoomBox.glb as a placeable speaker asset that can be cloned up to 5 instances. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at distance 8 looking at the shrine center, with ambient light intensity 0.4 and two directional lights for dramatic temple lighting. Draw five translucent colored circular zones on the ground around the shrine representing sacred acoustic regions, each with a target resonance value displayed as floating text sprites (values between 40-100 dB). Implement these interactions: (1) Click a toolbar Add Speaker button to spawn a BoomBox clone at a default position. (2) Drag-and-drop speakers to reposition them on the ground plane using raycasting. (3) Click a placed speaker to select it, showing a UI panel with coupled sliders for frequency (20-2000 Hz) and volume (0-100%). Frequency and volume are coupled so increasing frequency reduces max available volume proportionally. (4) A global energy conservation bar shows total system wattage capped at 300W; each speaker's wattage equals volume times a frequency multiplier. Prevent volume increases that would exceed the cap. (5) Each zone calculates received dB from all speakers using inverse-square distance falloff and displays it with color coding: green if within 5 dB of target, yellow within 15, red otherwise. (6) Implement undo/redo stack tracking all actions: placements, moves, slider changes, and deletions. Bind Ctrl+Z for undo and Ctrl+Shift+Z for redo. (7) Right-click a speaker to delete it, reclaiming its energy. (8) Add a Check Solution button that validates all five zones are green simultaneously. Display a congratulations modal with particle effects on success. (9) Show a real-time energy flow visualization as animated dotted lines from each speaker to zones it affects, with line opacity proportional to contribution. The task requires 10-14 steps minimum: adding speakers, positioning them, tuning sliders, checking energy budget, undoing mistakes, and verifying the solution.
